title: Microstate Snapshot Prefetch PRD — Variant Experiments and SDK Ergonomics
summary: Working PRD exploring a microstate snapshot + prefetch model for incremental streaming, tool bridging during partial results, and SDK ergonomics that make graceful fallback and structured output easier for integrators.
body:
Purpose and context:

This doc captures a set of small, intentionally divergent experiments (variants) for how Hosted API can expose and operate on microstate snapshots during streaming responses. The idea: provide compact, replayable checkpoints (microstate snapshots) that let SDKs prefetch tool results, resume partial structured output, and opt into fidelity tiers without re-running full model decoding.

Why we care (user problems):
- Product integrators want deterministic resume semantics for long-running streams (mobile clients, flaky networks).
- Tool-backed flows need a safe way to call external tools off partial output without committing to a final model completion.
- Customers want observable cost/latency tradeoffs for prefetch vs on-demand tool execution.
- SDK devs need ergonomic primitives so app teams can adopt progressive responses without custom orchestration.

High-level proposal (variants):

Variant A — Minimal snapshot envelope
- Server emits a tiny JSON "microstate" envelope at defined micro-turn boundaries (e.g., every 512 tokens or when a tool-intent appears). Envelope contains: session_id, turn_idx, stable_prefix_hash, tool_intents (list), partial_structured_frame (optional).
- SDKs store microstate; when connectivity resumes they request /resume?session_id=&turn_idx= to fetch delta tokens or rehydrate.
- Tool calling: SDKs may invoke tools based on tool_intents in the envelope; the server accepts tool results and synthesizes them into subsequent tokens.
- Tradeoffs: Low overhead, easy to implement, but requires consistent hashing semantics and careful schema versioning.

Variant B — Prefetch hint + speculative tool queue
- Server provides prefetch_hints with probabilities for tool intents and estimated token length. SDKs can speculatively request tool outputs from partner services (or local cache) with a TTL.
- If actual model path differs, server returns an abort signal and the prefetched result is discarded or used as a candidate for reranking.
- Upside: reduces perceived latency for common tool calls. Downside: extra cost, more complex billing/observability.

Variant C — Checkpoint + KV cache pointer
- Microstate is a pointer into a server-side checkpoint (opaque id). SDKs request 'materialize' for the checkpoint when needed; server streams only incremental tokens since checkpoint.
- Enables cheap resume and re-rollouts (A/B model variant comparisons) because checkpoints are reusable.
- Requires backend storage and retention policy (SLA implications).

Common requirements across variants:
- Schema versioning: microstate schemas must include schema_version and compatibility notes; SDKs should tolerate unknown fields.
- Observability: emit events for microstate creation, materialize requests, and prefetch abortions with correlation ids.
- Security: any pointer-based variant must include short-lived HMACs or server-side auth to avoid stale pointer misuse.
- Billing: prefetch operations must be tagged and separable in usage aggregation.

SDK ergonomics suggestions (developer-friendly primitives):
- MicrostateStore: simple interface (save(snapshot), load(session_id, turn_idx), list(session_id)). Keep sync and async variants.
- PrefetchPolicy: declarative config for when to prefetch (probability threshold, allowed tool domains, cost cap).
- ToolBridge.adapt(): helper to take a tool_intent from a microstate and normalize to common tool call shapes (http, sql, internal RPC).
- ResumeSession(session_id, opts): high-level call that hides pointer exchange, checkpoint materialize, and token diff application.

Tool calling semantics during partial streams:
- Tool intents in microstate are "suggestions" not commands — server decides final callability based on model state at commit.
- Design a small handshake: SDK announces intended tool result (id, sketch) and server replies with one of {accept, queue, reject, require-confirm}.
- For acceptance, server consumes the tool result into the ongoing generation. For queue, server keeps a short window and may request finalization if generation path requires it.

Structured output considerations:
- Microstate can contain partial structured frames (JSON fragments) and a stable prefix hash to detect drift when resuming.
- We must avoid divergent parse states: provide a compact "repair plan" mechanism where server can send small edit patches (JSON-patch or delta-ops) to bring client fragments into alignment.
- Backwards compatibility: SDKs should be able to fall back to text-only streams when structured fragment schema cannot be applied.

Operational & infra notes:
- Retention: default microstate retention 30 minutes for ephemeral sessions, opt-in longer retention for dedicated customers. Configurable per-route.
- Storage cost estimate: approximate 200B per microstate envelope on average; at N qps we calculate ~XGB/day (back-of-envelope to be added).
- Materialize load: materialize operations create read pressure — throttle per-account and surface error code 429.

Telemetry & acceptance metrics:
- Per-route microstate creation rate and size distribution.
- Prefetch hit-rate (prefetch that was used vs aborted).
- Resume latency reduction: median 50th/95th for resumed sessions compared to cold restart.
- Tool-call latency delta when prefetching vs on-demand.
- Error surface: % of resume failures where schema mismatch occurred.

Rollout plan (experimental phases):
- Phase 0 (lab): implement Variant A in toy runtime + SDK internal preview. Internal only, no billing. Goal: validate schema and debug resume paths.
- Phase 1 (alpha): enable Variant B prefetch hints for a small set of customers (opt-in). Collect prefetch cost telemetry.
- Phase 2 (beta): pointer-based checkpoints (Variant C) behind a feature flag for Dedicated customers; measure storage & materialize load.
- Phase 3 (GA): surface SDK primitives, docs, and clear billing semantics.

Acceptance criteria (minimal):
- Resume works for >95% of resumed sessions within the 30 minute retention window (no manual rehydration).
- Prefetch hit improves median tool-call latency by at least 80ms for targeted workflows.
- SDK APIs are under 6 thin calls for a common mobile resume flow (i.e., low cognitive load).

Open questions / risks (quick list):
- Schema drift when models change decoding behavior. Do we tie microstate versioning to model-version? Pros/cons.
- What is the right default prefetch probability? Risk: customers unexpectedly pay for prefetches.
- Edge clients: how to expose storage/eviction signals when SDK has limited local cache?
- Security: risk vectors for materialize pointer abuse and replay attacks.
- Instrumentation complexity: correlate microstate disco with token-level traces across backends.

Notes & experiments to run next sprint:
- A: implement minimal envelope for gpt-micro-demo and run 2 week internal hackathon on flaky network scenarios (mobile app).
- B: internal perf bench for prefetch cost vs latency win with a small tool set (search + code-exec).
- C: prototype repair-plan JSON-patch flow and test with existing structured-output use-cases (invoices, API manifests).

References / links:
- Related ideation: CONFLUENCE - session-resume-playbooks (see linked_artifacts)
- GitHub PR: hosted-sdk/pull/942 (early MicrostateStore types)
- Jira: JIRA-API-7219 (prefetch billing taxonomy)

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- This is intentionally exploratory: please push back on complexity vs benefit. If we take pointers (Variant C) we need a clear SLA and retention pricing model.
- Focus review on SDK ergonomics: are the primitives enough for a mobile-first flow?
- Try to surface one small, high-impact experiment we can ship to internal customers within 3 sprints.

Choppy to-do (for product + eng pairing):
- [ ] Marcus: sketch microstate JSON canonical shape, include schema_version and stable_prefix_hash.
- [ ] Evan: bench prefetch cost for search-type tools (100k sample).
- [ ] Sasha: draft SDK MicrostateStore API and a mobile sample (iOS/Android).
- [ ] Priya: write a short customer-facing note that explains opt-in prefetch billing.

End of draft.

(Notes to self: keep this doc lightweight; move finalized spec to Confluence and add longer examples/sequence diagrams there.)
